title: Hyderabad's average home now costs ₹2.15 crore, up ₹21 lakh in a year

slides.head: Hyderabad's average home now costs ₹2.15 crore, up ₹21 lakh in a year
What happened
slides.body: Average property value rose from ₹1.94 crore to ₹2.15 crore. Only Chennai saw a bigger jump (₹25 lakh); Bengaluru was third (₹19 lakh).

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: Industry players point to land costs and Hyderabad's no-cap FSI rule, which has pushed average flat size to around 2,000 sft vs 1,000-1,500 sft in Mumbai and Bengaluru.

slides.head: Did you know
slides.body: Hyderabad sold 13,270 homes in Q3 2026, down from 15,349 a year earlier.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether prices hold as unsold stock piles up, and the Q4 sales numbers. Ask: If sales are falling, why are prices still rising?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
Hyderabad's average home now costs ₹2.15 crore, up ₹21 lakh in a year

CRE Matrix-CREDAI data shows Hyderabad property prices rose 10.5% between Q3 2025 and Q3 2026, making it India's second-most expensive metro housing market after Delhi.

Why it matters: Industry players point to land costs and Hyderabad's no-cap FSI rule, which has pushed average flat size to around 2,000 sft vs 1,000-1,500 sft in Mumbai and Bengaluru.

Source: Times of India. Image: Times of India
